title: Relative boundary filling for symmetric operadic extension families
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, degreewise simplicial pullbacks and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], symmetric infinity-operads and inert-preserving maps of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], the active concatenation $\oplus$ of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation], and coherent slices with source projections of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Let $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be a cocartesian fibration and a map of symmetric infinity-operads. Let $\mathcal P^\otimes\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal Q^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be maps of small symmetric infinity-operads. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/\mathcal O^\otimes}(\mathcal P^\otimes,\mathcal E^\otimes)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/\mathcal O^\otimes}(\mathcal Q^\otimes,\mathcal E^\otimes)$: the full subcategories on inert-preserving functors, with all coherent transformations over $\mathcal O^\otimes$. Restriction is $u^*:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. The coherent comma quasicategory $\mathcal T$ of triples $(A,F,\eta:A\to u^*F)$ is modeled by
$$\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal A)\times_{\mathcal A,\operatorname{ev}_1,u^*}\mathcal B,$$
with source projection $r:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$ given by $\operatorname{ev}_0$. Its simplices retain the whole coherent family of these arrows and both endpoint algebra functors.

For a vertex $H=(A,F,\eta)$ and a color $d$ of $\mathcal Q$, put $J_d=\mathcal P^\otimes\times_{\mathcal Q^\otimes}(\mathcal Q^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/d}$ and let $D_d:J_d\to\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ be $A$ after source projection. The transformation $\eta$ and the arrows into $d$ induce an active coherent cocone $c_d:D_d\to\Delta_{J_d}F(d)$ with component $F(\alpha)\eta_p$ at $(p,\alpha:u(p)\to d)$. Say that $H$ satisfies the local condition if for every $d$, every $Z\in\mathcal E^\otimes$ and every $W\in\mathcal E^\otimes_{\langle1\rangle}$, restriction along $c_d\oplus1_Z$ gives a homotopy pullback square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}}(F(d)\oplus Z,W)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J_d,\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})}(D_d\oplus Z,\Delta_{J_d}W)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}}(q(F(d)\oplus Z),qW)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J_d,\mathcal O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})}(q(D_d\oplus Z),\Delta_{J_d}(qW)).
\end{array}$$
Here the vertical maps apply $q$ and the bottom map uses the specified base cocone $qc_d$; a homotopy pullback means equivalence with the path-space homotopy fiber product, retaining its specified composition homotopy. This is the mapping-space form of the operadic relative colimit condition, tested after every fixed concatenation; it is a condition on the given cocones, with no existence assertion.

For every $n>0$, suppose $b:\Delta^n\to\mathcal A$ and $h_0:\partial\Delta^n\to\mathcal T$ satisfy $rh_0=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$ exactly, and the vertex $h_0(0)$ satisfies the local condition. Then there exists $h:\Delta^n\to\mathcal T$ with $rh=b$ and $h|_{\partial\Delta^n}=h_0$ exactly. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of the proper faces of the standard simplex. No terminal-object, presentability or global colimit hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3.16, Remark 3.1.3.15 and the mapping-cylinder construction in the proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed pp. 346-348; mapping-space local condition from Definition 3.1.1.2 and Remark 3.1.1.5. September 18, 2017 edition inspected online; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic assertion.

proof.text: Choose $M=M_u^\otimes$, $t:M\to\Delta^1$, $g:M\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ and $R:\mathcal L\to\mathcal T$ from [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-mapping-cylinder]. Lift the given boundary $h_0$ to $\widetilde h_0:\partial\Delta^n\to\mathcal L$. Here is why its boundary-lifting assertion suffices: order the finitely many nondegenerate simplices of $\partial\Delta^n$ by dimension, first lift each vertex using its dimension-zero case, and then lift each simplex relative to its already fixed proper faces. Define degenerate simplices by degeneracy; all intersections are already fixed. Thus $R\widetilde h_0=h_0$ exactly. Let $\widetilde H=\widetilde h_0(0)$. The active-slice and specified-cocone clause identifies its colorwise local tests with the squares for $h_0(0)$ in the statement, so $\widetilde H$ satisfies the colorwise relative operadic left Kan condition of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. This transfers the given cocones, rather than asserting new colimits.

source.place: Remark 3.1.3.15 and mapping-cylinder construction in the proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, pp.346-348; strict relative lifting made explicit

proof.text: We will use categorical lifting for $q$. It is a Joyal fibration: take simplicial opposites, reversing the vertices in each simplex. The initial-horn and prescribed-source cocartesian conditions for $q$ become the final-horn and prescribed-target cartesian conditions for $q^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], this cartesian fibration over the quasicategory $(\mathcal O^\otimes)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a Joyal fibration. Reversing again preserves categorical equivalences: in the testing definition of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], $h\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},C)$ is $h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and an equivalence of categories remains one on taking opposites. Reversal also preserves degreewise injectivity and commutative lifting squares. Therefore the Joyal lifting property transfers from $q^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $q$. In particular $q$ lifts every degreewise injective categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 3.1.3.16, p.347, categorical-fibration lifting; opposite of the Cartesian-fibration criterion in HTT 3.1.1

proof.text:
Transpose $\widetilde h_0$ to a family map $M\times\partial\Delta^n\to\mathcal E^\otimes$. Transpose $b$ to $\mathcal P^\otimes\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E^\otimes$. They agree on $\mathcal P^\otimes\times\partial\Delta^n$, because source restriction commutes exactly with $R$. In the prism $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ let
$$K_0=(\Delta^n\times\{0\})\cup(\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1).$$
Their union is a map $f_0:K_0\times_{\Delta^1}M\to\mathcal E^\otimes$ over the fixed map to $\mathcal O^\otimes$ which forgets the $\Delta^n$ coordinate and applies $g$. This is a degreewise gluing of equal maps, so it preserves the entire given coherent boundary. All vertices of the prism already belong to $K_0$; their fiber restrictions are inert-preserving algebra functors.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3.16, p.347: initial prism subset and transposition of coherent diagrams

proof.text:
For $0\leq i\leq n$ put $k=n-i$ and let $\sigma_i:\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ have ordered vertices
$$(0,0),\ldots,(k,0),(k,1),\ldots,(n,1).$$
Inductively let $K_{i+1}=K_i\cup\sigma_i(\Delta^{n+1})$. Their union is the whole prism: a chain in $[n]\times[1]$ changes its second coordinate at most once, and extends to a maximal chain of this displayed form. The intersection of the new simplex with $K_i$ is exactly its horn $\Lambda_k^{n+1}$. To check faces, deleting a vertex other than the adjacent pair $(k,0),(k,1)$ omits its first-coordinate value and lies on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$; deleting $(k,1)$ is in the preceding simplex when $k<n$, and is the bottom face when $k=n$. The sole new face deletes $(k,0)$, its index $k$. This includes $k=0$, where the missing face is the top face, and all smaller intersections follow by restriction. Hence each attachment is a pushout of this horn. Pullback to $M$ preserves these unions and intersections degree by degree, so the same pushout describes the domain on which $f_i$ must be extended.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 3.1.3.16, p.347: explicit prism filtration and attaching horn, with intersection check

proof.text: Suppose $0\leq i<n$ and a compatible $f_i:K_i\times_{\Delta^1}M\to\mathcal E^\otimes$ has been constructed. Then $1\leq k=n-i\leq n$, so $\Lambda_k^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$ is an inner horn inclusion and is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-categorical-base-change] with $S=\Delta^1$, $Z=M$, $r=t$, $B=\Delta^{n+1}$ and base map the second coordinate of $\sigma_i$. It makes the actual pulled-back horn inclusion a categorical equivalence. It is degreewise injective as well. Step 2 and the lifting property in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] therefore extend $f_i$ over this cell with its boundary and its map to $\mathcal O^\otimes$ fixed. Glue this lift to $f_i$ to obtain $f_{i+1}$. The lifts preserve inert edges of the family: over the ordered base simplex an inert edge has constant parameter, and its fiber restriction is one of the already fixed vertex algebra functors from step 3. This proves the induction from $f_0$ to $f_n$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 3.1.3.16, p.347, inner cells; HA Lemma 2.4.4.6 replaced by the existing stronger cocartesian base-change theorem for this chosen cylinder

proof.text: The remaining cell is $\sigma_n$, with vertices $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1),\ldots,(n,1)$ and missing horn $\Lambda_0^{n+1}$. Its pullback $N=M\times_{\Delta^1}\Delta^{n+1}$ is a symmetric operadic family by [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-mapping-cylinder]. Since $n>0$, its dimension $n+1$ is at least two. The first edge restricts to $M$ over the fixed first coordinate $0$, and the already prescribed map on it is exactly $\widetilde H$. Step 1 gives its colorwise relative operadic left Kan condition. All the other horn faces have already been prescribed by $f_n$, and its base map is the restriction of $g$. Thus [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-left-horn-filling] extends over this cell with exactly these restrictions. Glue to $f_n$. This gives a family map $f:M\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E^\otimes$ over $g$, whose source restriction is $b$ and whose boundary is $\widetilde h_0$, both exactly. The dimension-one case of the item uses this same argument: the first cell fills an inner $2$-horn and the last an operadic zeroth $2$-horn.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 3.1.3.16, p.347, final cell via Theorem 3.1.2.3(B), p.330

proof.text: Transpose $f$ to $\widetilde h:\Delta^n\to\mathcal L$ and put $h=R\widetilde h$. By the strict source compatibility of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-mapping-cylinder], $rh=b$. Restriction commutes with transposition and with $R$, so $h|_{\partial\Delta^n}=R\widetilde h_0=h_0$. This is a filler in the comma model specified in the statement, with all coherent transformations and their faces retained. No vertex or face has been replaced by an equivalent one.
